comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center net revenue increased 94% to $12.6 billion in 2024 from $6.5 billion in 2023, primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs. Operating income rose to $3.5 billion in 2024 from $1.3 billion in 2023, mainly due to higher revenue partially offset by increased R&D investment.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies address the competitive dynamics within the data center sector, specifically regarding the relationship with cloud service providers (hyperscalers). Intel identifies the 'increasing shift of data center workloads to the public cloud' as a driver that heightens the purchasing power of hyperscalers and increases competition, noting that the competitive environment 'adversely affected our results'. AMD discloses that its Data Center segment, which serves these same cloud environments, experienced significant growth (94% revenue increase) driven by sales of its GPUs and CPUs to these customers. While both acknowledge the critical importance of hyperscalers in the data center market, Intel frames the relationship through the lens of competitive pressure and customer concentration risk, whereas AMD highlights the financial success and scale of revenue generated from this specific customer base.

sentences.text: Industry trends, such as the increasing shift of data center workloads to the public cloud, have increased the significance and purchasing power of certain customers, particularly hyperscalers, in some of our data center-focused businesses.
We are operating in an increasingly competitive environment, including serving cloud service provider customers, and the competitive environment adversely affected our results in the last few years.
Data Center net revenue of $12.6 billion in 2024 increased by 94%, compared to net revenue of $6.5 billion in 2023.
The increase was primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center customer segments and automotive demand outlook
comparisons.peer_summary: In the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2024, large cloud providers represented more than half of Data Center revenue. Additionally, the company expects NVIDIA's automotive data center processing demand to grow significantly as AV algorithms shift to video transformers.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose the dominance of large cloud providers as a primary revenue driver in the data center segment. Intel explicitly states that industry trends have increased the significance and purchasing power of 'hyperscalers' (cloud service providers), creating a competitive environment where these customers are key. NVIDIA corroborates the materiality of this customer group by stating that 'large cloud providers represented more than half of our Data Center revenue' in Q4 2024. Both disclosures center on the strategic importance of hyperscale cloud customers to the data center business, though Intel emphasizes the competitive pressure exerted by their purchasing power, while NVIDIA quantifies their share of revenue.

sentences.text: Industry trends, such as the increasing shift of data center workloads to the public cloud, have increased the significance and purchasing power of certain customers, particularly hyperscalers, in some of our data center-focused businesses.
In the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2024, large cloud providers represented more than half of our Data Center revenue, supporting both internal workloads and external customers.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm expects continued intense competition, partly driven by vertical integration by certain customers, such as Apple.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Qualcomm disclose risks related to customers vertically integrating and developing their own components, which intensifies competition for the semiconductor supplier. Intel warns that 'some cloud service provider customers have also internally developed, and may continue to develop, their own semiconductors,' which can lead to order changes or cancellations. Qualcomm similarly identifies 'vertical integration by certain of our customers (e.g., Apple)' as a source of 'continued intense competition.' Both disclosures highlight the specific business risk of hyperscaler or major OEM customers bypassing external suppliers by designing in-house silicon, thereby threatening the supplier's market share and revenue stability.

sentences.text: Some cloud service provider customers have also internally developed, and may continue to develop, their own semiconductors, including designs customized for their specific computing workloads.

The further consolidation of computing workloads in the cloud, and consolidation among cloud service providers, can heighten the competitive importance of factors such as collaboration and customization with cloud service provider customers to optimize products for their environments; optimization for cloud services and applications; product performance; energy efficiency; feature differentiation; product quality, reliability, and factors affecting server uptime; and product security and security features.
• We expect continued intense competition, including from vertical integration by certain of our customers (e.g., Apple).
